notes.9: Many candidates still insist on changing angles in radians to angles in degrees when attempting a question of this nature. This practice needs to be discouraged as it can lead to accuracy errors, incorrect use of formulae and also to giving an answer in an incorrect form. (i) When showing an angle is a certain value correct to 3 significant figures, it is expected that calculations are performed to a greater accuracy so that a correct conclusion can be made. Many candidates did not show that the angle was 2.352 radians or better. This was required in order to gain both marks. (ii) Most candidates were able to obtain a correct angle. (iii) Very few correct solutions were seen. Most candidates were able to find the length of the arc subtended by the angle PAQ , but many fewer candidates were able to find the length of the arc subtended by the angle PBQ , in spite of having just found this angle in part (ii) . (iv) Marks for the correct area of either a sector or a triangle and a correct plan were obtained by most. However, many solutions were muddled, with candidates not setting their solutions out clearly. Poor accuracy also led to a loss of marks. As a result, very few completely correct solutions were seen.
